paper_metadata.title: Effect of mechanical alloying on microstructure and mechanical properties of hot-pressed Nb–16Si alloys

evidence.quote: Effect of mechanical alloying on microstructure and mechanical properties of hot-pressed Nb–16Si alloys
Nb–16 at.% Si bulk alloys were fabricated by hot pressing from compound powders milled for different times.
A powder mixture with 47.28 g of Nb and 2.72 g of Si was added to each vial to obtain the nominal composition of Nb–16Si.
Nb–16Si alloys, ‘HA’, ‘HB’ and ‘HC’ were fabricated by hot pressing from compound powders milled for 6, 12 and 24 h, respectively.

The fracture toughness of bulk alloys decreased with the elongation of milling time because of the reduction in volume fraction of ductile Nbss phase. As for the investigated alloys of this study, the improvement of fracture toughness was mainly attributed to the mechanism of ductile-phase toughening.

As for the investigated alloys of this study, the improvement of fracture toughness was mainly attributed to the mechanism of ductile-phase toughening. Moreover, the present fracture toughness was higher than that of as-casted materials, and it resulted from both ductile-phase toughening and ﬁne-grain toughening.
Moreover, the mechanism of ﬁne-grain strengthening was also thought to contribute to the improved strength of materials made from powders milled for the longer time.

conflicts.topic: Effect of milling time on volume fraction of Nbss
conflicts.claim_1: With milling time increasing, the volume fraction of ductile Nbss decreased. (Abstract)
conflicts.claim_2: In addition, the volume fraction of ductile Nbss increased with the ball milling proceeding, while the change of silicides contrasted. (Conclusions)

evidence.quote: When milling time increased from 6 to 24 h, the constituent phases (Nbss, Nb5Si3 and Nb3Si) changed from large size trips to ﬁne near-equiaxed shape, and the volume fraction of ductile Nbss decreased.
In addition, the volume fraction of ductile Nbss increased with the ball milling proceeding, while the change of silicides contrasted.
